items.title: Earl Humphrey Interview, 1963-03-28
items.q: And Louis being such a good monopolist. Louis, too, man, he was a great guy. He knew how to handle anything. And he'd get in front of her and tell her when to stop and breathe.

ctx.x: What were you saying about the Ann Cook record? I didn't get that, you know. About her phrasing and stuff?

Yeah, we had to work with her, you know. Get out on time and phrasing the blues, you know, on time. Oh, yeah. I had to work with her for a while, see. Mm-hmm. And Louis being such a good monopolist. Louis, too, man, he was a great guy. He knew how to handle anything. And he'd get in front of her and tell her when to stop and breathe. Pull her right in on it, you know, next phrase.

items.title: Earl Humphrey Interview, 1968-11-30
items.q: like, well, Louis Domaine, who was playing with, and Sam Morgan's band

ctx.x: We had to change. It had to change. Not to my family. Yeah. Not the real old players have changed the style. No. But the young people have changed some of the styles of playing, such as the blues, Marlick Jazz, Rocky Roo.

Oh, yeah. Some other kind of a... But now, the thing is, if you listen to some of those old records, now this is what... I just have to go by the records, you see. But if you listen to those bands, now they only recorded a few of the bands down here, like, well, Louis Domaine, who was playing with, and Sam Morgan's band. Celestan. Celestan, yes. Celestan. Of course, the Perron Orchestra. Well, let's just take the Morgan band. To me, the Morgan band sounds to me like the style is nearly the same, but it's not…

Well, you know what I believe, and you don't make the difference. See, it's more modern equipment now for recording than it was then. Yeah. You get a... You can get better reception on what you're playing, you know, off of this modern equipment, than you could then. Yeah. That makes a big difference, see. They can phrase your music like they want on one of those, you know, regular recording of phrases. Well, before they didn't have all that.
